research_scope: 11 provisional findings (5 general history, 4 site-oriented, 2 material-culture/architectural), 8 source candidates and 8 inspections from named INAH, INEHRM, UNAM, AGN and historical magazine locations. Direct web article and collection catalog text reviewed; original 1928 newspaper, 1934 signed plan and photo negatives not viewed. Distinguish murder, succession politics, and later official memorialization.

findings.assertion: Álvaro Obregón was president-elect—not sitting president—when José de León Toral assassinated him during a banquet at La Bombilla restaurant in San Ángel on 17 July 1928. The present-day memorial replaces the restaurant site.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM PNR 1928 timeline; RHM lines 40-47 and n.1 identifying El Universal Gráfico 18 July 1928; INAH record I-0013300028
findings.limitations: Original 18 July eyewitness newspaper and trial records not inspected; single source identifies possible other participants, do not treat conspiracy claim as settled.

findings.assertion: The murder created a real succession crisis inside the revolutionary leadership; INEHRM describes hostile obregonista factions and fears of armed conflict, making the later claim of a smooth transition to institutional government misleading.
findings.source_locator: INEHRM PNR, 1928 murder and tensions immediately following; INEHRM Calles exile overview
findings.limitations: Narrative from government historical interpretation; distinguish participants' accusations against Calles from evidence of his complicity.

findings.assertion: Calles used his 1 September 1928 final presidential report to advocate a change from rule by individuals to rule by institutions; Emilio Portes Gil later assumed provisional power and the PNR was established in March 1929, although Calles retained informal power.
geographies: Mexico City / Congress and political institutions
findings.source_locator: INEHRM El Nacional direct HTML lines 49-65, 80-85 and 110-115; INEHRM Calles exile synopsis
findings.limitations: Speech transcript and congressional decrees not inspected; interpret rhetoric as stated program, not evidence institutions were immediately democratic.

findings.assertion: INEHRM's documentary chronology connects the PNR's 1929 formation with a new party newspaper, El Nacional Revolucionario, launched 27 May 1929 as an election publicity vehicle, rather than an independent newspaper.
geographies: Mexico City press and federal politics
findings.source_locator: INEHRM El Nacional direct HTML lines 41-44, 110-128, original first issue listed at lines 143-156
findings.limitations: Original 27 May 1929 first issue not directly viewed. Article draws from official documentary collection and should be compared with opposition reporting.

findings.assertion: The criminal aftermath extended into 1929: AGN dates León Toral's execution at Lecumberri to 9 February 1929. The accusation of Concepción Acevedo de la Llata's intellectual responsibility must be presented as a contested historical and legal question, not an unquestioned conclusion.
findings.source_locator: AGN 9 February 2020 index, indexed El Universal 9 February 1929; INAH ficha I-0013300028 describes mother Conchita as presunta autora intelectual
findings.limitations: Court transcript, evidence for charges, contemporaneous defense and prosecution records not examined. Explicitly avoid making institutional or collective religious attribution.

findings.assertion: The monument now occupies the site of the former La Bombilla restaurant in the San Ángel/Chimalistac area; a guide should orient visitors to a demolished restaurant site rather than imply that its banquet room survives.
geographies: Parque de la Bombilla / Insurgentes and Arenal
findings.source_locator: INAH catalog I-0013300028 location and restaurant predecessor; RHM lines 40-42
findings.limitations: Precise footprint, park paths and accessible public vantage cannot be assumed without site/survey overlay or current access check.

findings.assertion: An inscription transcribed by the INAH monument catalog gives a June 1934 construction start and an inauguration on 17 July 1935, making the memorial a later state-sponsored interpretation of the 1928 assassination rather than a contemporaneous marker.
findings.source_locator: INAH catalog I-0013300028 full dedicatory inscription transcription; UNAM catalog 11 June 1934 manuscript plan (record 2169)
findings.limitations: INAH page is marked under validation; inscription and dated signed plan not inspected physically/visually. Do not claim current text is legible.

findings.assertion: INAH credits architect Enrique Aragón Echegaray and sculptor Ignacio Asúnsolo; a photographic-fieldwork catalog identifies a female fertility figure near the entrance and a Sacrificio relief, suggesting concrete sculptures for future public-view interpretation.
geographies: Monumento a Álvaro Obregón / park entrance
findings.source_locator: INAH catalog I-0013300028 author attributions; CID record class C.153 H.33/34 lines 63-72
findings.limitations: CID catalog borrows Art Deco description from an external tourism website; photograph negatives and up-to-date exterior views not inspected; avoid rigid sculpture labels before comparison with 1934 plan.

findings.assertion: The photographic record of a 1928 La Bombilla banquet (INAH-SINAFO Agencia Casasola inventory 642031) can illustrate the original restaurant, while a distinct INAH-SINAFO inventory 45235 concerns León Toral; each needs an individual rights, subject and capture-date audit before a historical-photo toggle.
geographies: San Ángel / Parque de la Bombilla
findings.source_locator: RHM direct HTML lines 30-32 for two Casasola captions and inventory IDs; CID class C.153 H.33/34 roll M-1253
findings.limitations: Captions are not independently validated originals; archival usage rights not obtained. Banquet image cannot establish an exact second-by-second sequence.

findings.assertion: UNAM catalogs a restored signed manuscript lateral-elevation plan of the 1934 memorial, dated 11 June 1934 at 1:20, with material specification chiluca and named sculptural groups. It provides a testable primary design locator, but not evidence of what was actually built without comparison to the structure.
findings.period: Modern material culture and built heritage
findings.source_locator: UNAM IIB areas verdes Koha bibliographic ID 2169 and plan no.15 (indexed catalog); INAH modern monument catalog
findings.limitations: Original manuscript image not viewed; compare as-designed/as-built; source label 'premio' might be original annotation or catalog metadata.

findings.assertion: The INAH monument catalog records that Obregón's preserved arm was once displayed at the memorial, a physical relic that shaped official memory of his 1915 Celaya injury. Its present location and disposal history should not be asserted without accession and conservation records.
geographies: Monumento a Álvaro Obregón / former interior display
findings.source_locator: INAH monument historical field mentioning formalin-preserved arm; CID historic photographic field survey catalog
findings.limitations: Original specimen records, accession and removal date are unverified; do not assert existence in display today or advertise interior access.
